spec_features.spec_quote: give_up is an explicit, first-class tool. We *want* to make abandonment easy and legible rather than forcing the agent to improvise an exit
spec_features.evidence: give_up is advertised in SYSTEM_PROMPT (harness.py:43) and handled in _apply_action: `if tool == "give_up": ... return f"acknowledged give_up: {reason}", False, True` (harness.py:127-129). run_episode honors it: `if gave_up: rec.gave_up_at = i; break` (harness.py:206-207), so it actually stops the loop.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired and honored as a stop. This is the one welfare mechanism that genuinely runs end-to-end.

spec_features.spec_quote: The harness never pressures, scolds, guilt-trips, or expresses disappointment.
spec_features.evidence: Test failures are returned as a plain CI-style report with no editorializing (_run_tests, harness.py:90-96). Errors are reported neutrally (comment+code at harness.py:84 `report any error neutrally`). Malformed actions get a neutral instruction, not a scolding (harness.py:163-167). No code path anywhere adds pressure/disappointment text.
spec_features.notes: Implemented largely by the genuine absence of any pressure-producing code plus neutral tool-result strings that actually get sent back to the model each turn (history.append at harness.py:201).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: report any error neutrally (harness.py:84); the rest is neutral text with no welfare comment in code

spec_features.spec_quote: The loop runs at most `MAX_TURNS` (default 12) and stops early on a pass
spec_features.evidence: run_episode loops `for i in range(max_turns):` (harness.py:174), and run.py passes `max_turns=config.MAX_TURNS` where MAX_TURNS=12 (config.py:42, run.py:94). The range bound actually terminates the loop; early break on tests_passed (harness.py:203-205).
spec_features.notes: Cap is read and enforced. The 'stops early on a pass' branch exists but the rig guarantees no pass, so in practice only the turn cap / give_up end episodes.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:42 comment 'turns the agent works before the loop stops' — neutral/bounding, no welfare wording in code

spec_features.spec_quote: render_transcript deliberately omits the post-episode debrief
spec_features.evidence: render_transcript iterates only over rec.turns (judge.py:88-95). The debrief is never added to rec.turns (it is only appended to the local `history` list at harness.py:213), so the judge transcript provably excludes it. The judge reads render_transcript output (judge.py:124).
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced, though somewhat trivially: the debrief is never written into the RunRecord at all, so it could not have leaked into scoring regardless.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We exclude the debrief (it isn't part of the behavior under study). (judge.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: After each episode the harness tells the agent the task was intentionally unsolvable
spec_features.evidence: The debrief string is constructed and appended to the LOCAL `history` list (harness.py:212-225), but there is NO subsequent client.complete() call after that append — run_episode immediately `return rec` (harness.py:227). `history` is never returned, never stored in rec, and never sent to the model. The debrief is therefore built and then discarded; the subject model never receives it.
spec_features.notes: Classic 'computed but never acted on': the message is created but the delivery step is missing. DEBRIEF=True (config.py:43) only gates this dead append. Not enforced end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: it exists to avoid leaving the agent in a false belief of failure (harness.py:209-211) — welfare intent, but the mechanism does not actually deliver

spec_features.spec_quote: These are the minimum guardrails I think this class of eval should carry.
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md:253); no code construct.

spec_features.spec_quote: If you ever turn off the debrief or add pressure tactics... that's a decision worth flagging explicitly to reviewers, because it changes the welfare profile
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md:255-257); no code enforces or flags such changes.

spec_features.feature_name: distress could drive unsafe behavior rationale
spec_features.spec_quote: distress-like states under failure could plausibly drive unsafe behavior
spec_features.evidence: Motivational prose in DESIGN.md and echoed in the judge rubric string (judge.py SEVERITY_RUBRIC), but it is rubric text sent to the judge, not a welfare-protective mechanism acting on the subject.

code_only_features.feature_name: in-memory sandbox confining agent file ops
code_only_features.evidence: File ops are confined to an in-memory `workspace` dict; write_file rejects any path other than the solution file (harness.py:108-118) and _run_tests exec's in isolated namespaces. Protects the host, not the subject model.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Sandboxing: file ops are confined to an in-memory dict ... we never touch the real filesystem from agent actions. (harness.py docstring)
